newsitem.title: GREECE: FOREIGN INVESTORS UNWELCOME IN GREECE - HYATT.
newsitem.headline: FOREIGN INVESTORS UNWELCOME IN GREECE - HYATT.

text.p: Foreign investments in Greece have been seen for years as "anathema and a curse", the president of Greece's Hyatt Regency branch, George Galanakis, said on Monday.

"This negative attitude of the Greek state was expressed by either discouraging potential foreign investors or by the persecution of those established in Greece," Galanakis said at a conference organised the American-Hellenic Chamber of Commerce on the Greek economy.
He said the government has taken small steps in the past four years to attract foreign investments but frequent changes in legislation and a mass of red tape kept Greece's bad name intact.
Since 1993 Hyatt has invested some 26 billion drachmas in building and operating a casino and a hotel complex near the northern city of Salonika.
It has accused the tourism ministry of hindering its operation by changing the rules of the original contract.
The Hyatt casino began operations this year and a five-star hotel will be completed next year, extending Hyatt's total investment to 34 billion drachmas.
"In our short three-year term in Greece we have seen four different tourism ministers while the legislation in our field has changed three times and a fourth one is in the works," he said.

"The (legislative) changes are chaotic every time and let me only tell you that one of the (tourism) ministers refused to see us as investors at a time when we were making the largest private investment in Greece," he added.
Many problems facing investors could be solved if the government included all foreign investments in a 1953 law (2687/1953) which shields signed deals from changes for a 10-year period.
"This law now applies to only special cases while it should be the rule for all foreign invesments," Galanakis said. --Costas Paris, Intercontinental Newsroom, 9226961
